newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks tips from Reagan's 1984 debates.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks tips from Reagan's 1984 debates.

text.p: President Bill Clinton has been studying the 1984 debates between President Ronald Reagan and Democratic challenger Walter Mondale for clues on how Reagan was able to win a second term in the White House.

"We've said for some time that we thought the 1984 Reagan campaign was just a brilliant example of the re-election of an incumbent," Clinton's deputy campaign manager, Ann Lewis, told CNN from Chautauqua, New York, where Clinton was preparing for Sunday's presidential debate.

"And we tried to find some ideas for that in our structure. So as we put debate preparation together -- as the president started watching previous debates -- among them ... were the 1984 Reagan debates," Lewis said.
Clinton squares off against Republican Bob Dole in the first of two 90-minute presidential debates in Hartford, Connecticut, at 9 p.m. EDT Sunday (0100 GMT Monday).
